blog.title: I GOT A RIBBON!!! (the county fair report)
blog.body: ms. keller made me enter the county fair art show and i said but i only draw horses and she said 'so draw a horse.' so i did a different thing: a field of tall grass with the wind blowing through it so the grass makes the shape of a horse running. there is no horse in it. it's ALL horse. it took 9 days and the spray can tool was not allowed (ms. keller said 'not this one') so it was pencil. it was hard. i cried a little on day 4. on the day of the fair there were 61 pictures and mine was between a barn and a different barn. it got a pink ribbon: Honorable Mention. the judge's card said 'very enthusiastic.' i've read it 40 times. my mom says it's the nicest word. i think she's right. patrick can see the horse. so can chad. so can i. ok bye!!

blog.title: HOW TO BRAID A MANE (AND A HEAD) (a tutorial)
blog.body: step 1: brush it. (the hair, not the horse, unless u have a horse, then both.) step 2: part it into 3 equal parts. step 3: right over middle, left over middle, right over middle. say it out loud, it helps. (my cousin says it sounds like a spell. it IS a spell.) step 4: add a little hair from the side each time, like a river taking in a creek. step 5: tie it with something that's not a rubber band (a ribbon, yarn, in an emergency a pipe cleaner). step 6: say 'u look like a champion.' that's the main step. real show horses get tiny round braids called buttons and they're my favorite thing in the world. i can do a french braid in 90 seconds. i did 14 heads this month. ashley (the cheer captain) asked if i could make one survive a pyramid. i said challenge accepted. (pipe cleaner at the end. just in case.)

blog.title: PUMPKIN (what happened on visit #5)
blog.body: so the stable has an old pony named Pumpkin who bites. ms. dolores (she owns the stable) said 'he's not mean, he's just particular.' she told me he likes people who are quiet. i can't be quiet. i said OK. i sat on an overturned bucket. i didn't say anything. not 'hi.' not 'Pumpkin.' i held my carrot in my lap (ONE carrot) and just breathed. it was 40 minutes. my mom timed it. it felt like a year. at minute 38 he walked over. at minute 39 he put his chin on my shoulder. i did NOT move. he breathed in my ear for a whole minute. then he took the carrot, very gently, like it was a secret. ms. dolores said 'well' and nothing else. in the car i said 'i'm never going to be quiet again' and mom said 'that's fine, but it was nice to see.' i drew him that night. he has no sparkles. it's the first one i didn't use the spray can on. he doesn't need it.

blog.title: WHAT I DO WHEN THERE'S NO HORSE AVAILABLE (a list)
blog.body: 1) draw one. 2) draw one for somebody else. 3) walk dogs at the shelter on sundays (i've walked Waffles 3 times, he's a beagle, he isn't a horse but he has the same energy about snacks). 4) braid something. 5) cartwheels in the yard (my record is 2 in a row, a cartwheel is basically a horse going sideways). 6) read about horses. 7) sit with my breyers and tell them about my day. (they have ears. they never say anything. best listeners.) 8) clean the breyers with a toothbrush, 1 per month, in order. 9) look at the sky until a cloud looks like a horse. (it takes 4 minutes on average. i timed it. there's always one.) 10) tell my mom the horse thing i learned today. she says 'that's wonderful, meg' every time, in a different voice, and i've decided she's really listening. ok bye!!
